_meta.indication: ELIQUIS (apixaban) is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, double-dummy comparison with warfarin titrated to a target INR of 2-3, designed to demonstrate non-inferiority on a composite endpoint of stroke and systemic embolism; patients followed for a median of 89 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation; mean age 69 years, 43% vitamin K antagonist (VKA) naive.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: composite rate of stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic) and systemic embolism (noninferiority to warfarin, with superiority also examined).
pivotal_trials.n: 18,201 randomized (9120 apixaban, 9081 warfarin in ITT analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: Stroke/systemic embolism (ITT): 212/9120 apixaban vs 265/9081 warfarin, HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66, 0.95), p=0.0114 (superiority). Major bleeding: HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.60, 0.80), p<0.0001. All-cause death: 603 vs 669, HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.80, 1.00), p=0.0465.

nct_ctgov.title: Apixaban for the Prevention of Stroke in Subjects With Atrial Fibrillation

key_safety: The most serious and most common adverse reactions are related to bleeding. In ARISTOTLE, major bleeding occurred in 327 (2.13%/year) apixaban patients vs 462 (3.09%/year) warfarin patients (HR 0.69); intracranial bleeding 0.33% vs 0.82% (HR 0.41). Bleeding-related discontinuation occurred in 1.7% (apixaban) vs 2.5% (warfarin).
target_moa: Apixaban is an oral, reversible, and selective active site inhibitor of Factor Xa (FXa); it does not require antithrombin III for activity, inhibits free and clot-bound FXa and prothrombinase activity, thereby decreasing thrombin generation and thrombus development.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DISCONTINUING ELIQUIS IN PATIENTS WITHOUT ADEQUATE CONTINUOUS ANTICOAGULATION INCREASES RISK OF STROKE. Discontinuing ELIQUIS places patients at an increased risk of thrombotic events; an increased rate of stroke was observed following discontinuation in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, and coverage with another anticoagulant should be strongly considered.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved at original approval.

advisory_committee.vote: The application for ELIQUIS was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class and in the intended population.

description.text: Added new indication for prophylaxis of DVT, which may lead to PE, in adults who have undergone hip or knee replacement surgery

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication for the prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) which may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE), in adult patients who have undergone hip or knee replacement surgery.

description.text: Added treatment of DVT and PE, and reduction in risk of recurrent DVT and PE following initial therapy

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for the following new indications: for the treatment of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and for the reduction in the risk of recurrent DVT and PE following initial therapy.

description.text: Added new pediatric indication for treatment of VTE and reduction in risk of recurrent VTE in patients from birth and older after at least 5 days of initial anticoagulant treatment

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for the addition of a new pediatric indication for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and reduction in the risk of recurrent VTE in pediatric patients from birth and older after at least 5 days of initial anticoagulant treatment, and for the addition of 0.5 mg tablets for oral suspension.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA approved based on ARISTOTLE; the application first received a Complete Response on 6/22/12 (dispensing-error concern), was resubmitted 9/17/2012, and approved with a REMS communication plan; it was not referred to an advisory committee.

The September 17, 2012, submission constituted a complete response to our June 22, 2012, action letter.

basis.text: The CR was issued primarily because of concern that a substantial fraction of patients might have been given the wrong treatment (active drug instead of placebo or vice versa), i.e., an apparent high rate of dispensing errors (7.3% of apixaban vs 1.2% of warfarin patients).

citations.quote: NDA 202155 was submitted on 9/28/2011 and was given a CR on 6/22/12, primarily because of concern with the finding that a substantial fraction of patients might have been given the wrong treatment (active drug instead of placebo or vice versa).
